methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort with PSM balancing baseline characteristics (SMD<0.05). 300 patients screened, 240 included post-matching with 36.2-month median follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models with Schoenfeld residuals confirmation. Post-hoc power analysis (80% for observed HR 0.69). Sensitivity analysis with IPW and multiple imputation. Thorough statistical approach.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Directly informs treatment selection for locally advanced cervical cancer. 3D-printed template-guided brachytherapy shows 9.2% OS improvement (76.7% vs 66.2%, p=0.02) and 11.7% LC improvement (90.0% vs 78.3%). Reduced severe toxicity (4.2% vs 11.7% Grade ≥3 proctitis). High clinical impact for treatment planning.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive Methods describing study design, patient selection, treatment protocols in detail enabling reproducibility. Complete Results with baseline characteristics, dosimetric outcomes, survival curves, subgroup analyses. Bonferroni correction applied to multiple subgroups. Data availability statement absent.

novelty_literature.justification: Application of 3D-printed template-guided brachytherapy to LACC is innovative. Demonstrates superiority over conventional freehand technique with robust dosimetric and clinical endpoints. Represents technical advance combining known technology (3D printing, brachytherapy) in novel application.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally detailed Methods section clearly describing 3D template design, fabrication, quality assurance, and intraoperative execution. Results logically organized with appropriate tables and Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion contextualizes within EMBRACE-I and other landmark studies. Figures effectively communicate dosimetric and survival outcomes.

key_strengths: PSM effectively balances all baseline characteristics (SMD<0.05); resectability subgroup analysis minimizes allocation bias from preferential assignment of complex tumors to 3D-PTIB
Substantial 36.2-month median follow-up with robust survival outcomes (OS, PFS, LC) and toxicity assessment
Dose-response analysis with restricted cubic splines demonstrates plateau effect above 85 Gy, providing mechanistic insight
Multivariable Cox regression confirms treatment modality remains independent predictor after adjusting for stage, diameter, chemotherapy completion
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability; prospective multicenter RCT needed for definitive comparison
Imaging heterogeneity: MRI-based planning for 3D-PTIB vs CT-based for F-3DIB may introduce systematic bias in HR-CTV delineation
Contingency planning for 5.3% of patients (hybrid/EBRT boost) somewhat ad-hoc; results may not apply to all LACC cases
chief_reviewer.rationale: Exceptionally well-conducted retrospective study demonstrating significant clinical benefit of 3D-printed template-guided brachytherapy for LACC. PSM and resectability subgroup analysis mitigate confounding. Robust dosimetric and survival outcomes with mature follow-up. Tier 2 appropriate for methodologic quality and clinical impact, though single-center design and lack of external validation preclude Tier 1.
